title: Efficient and Inexpensive Transient Expression of Multispecific Multivalent Antibodies in Expi293 Cells
author: Fang, Sehlin, et al.
materials: The cloned plasmid DNA was transfected to TOP10 cells (ThermoFisher) according to the instructions provided with the cells. Various kits were used to purify plasmid DNA, for instance GeneJET endo-free plasmid maxiprep (ThermoFisher), GeneJET Plasmid maxiprep (ThermoFisher) and QIAGENs maxiprep kit. The transfected bacteria were amplified in the recommended liquid medium (with ampicillin) and the plasmid purified according to the instructions for the plasmid purification kit used. The concentration was measured on a microvolume spectrophotometer (DeNovix DS-11). The DNA preparation should have an absorbance A260/A280 ratio of >1.8 to be considered clean enough for transfection.

The cells in the culture were counted. 1000 mvc will ultimately give 1 l of transfected cells. The cells were spun at 200 x g for 10 min at RT. The medium was removed by carefully decanting or by aspiration. To reduce shear forces during the transfection, Pluronic® F-68 (A1288.0100, VWR) is added to the transfection medium, which was made by addition of Pluronic® F-68 to the Expi293 medium for an end concentration of 0.1% Pluronic® F-68. The cells were resuspended in the transfection medium at a final concentration of 20 mvc/ml, i.e. if the total number of cells were 1000 mvc, the cells were diluted in 50 ml transfection medium in. A suitable flask size for this transfection was 125 ml. 1.25 mg of plasmid DNA per 1000 mvc was added to the culture (can be added to the resuspension flask during the spin to make this step more efficient). When expressing antibodies, which have the heavy and light chain expressed on different plasmids, the total amount of DNA added should still be 1.25 mg. 70% of the DNA for the light chain plasmid and 30% for the heavy chain plasmid were routinely used. When the DNA and cells had been mixed, 3.75 ml per 1000 mvc of 1 mg/ml of linear 40 kDa PEI Max (24765–1, Polysciences) solution was added (see materials for preparation instructions) and the cells were incubated under standard conditions for 3 h. After incubation, the cells were transferred to a larger flask and diluted with pre-warmed Expi293 medium to a concentration of 1 mvc/ml (i.e. if the total number of cells was 1000 mvc, 950 ml pre-warmed Expi293 media was added to the 50 ml transfection culture). 0.5 M VPA (P4543, Sigma Aldrich) (see materials for preparation instructions) was added to a final concentration of 3.5 mM (i.e. if the total number of cells was 1000 mvc in 1 l, then 7 ml of 0.5 M VPA was added). The transfected cells were incubated for 7–12 days at 37°C, 125 rpm, 8% CO2 atmosphere without handling them.

Companies that sell the different types of HEK293 cells usually promote variants of transfectamine as transfection reagents. Transfectamine and its variants are always expensive (approximately a thousand time more expensive than PEI). Transfection of Expi293 cells is routinely performed with ExpiFectamine transfection reagent. For expression of multiple variants of antibodies or large scale expression, the cost can easily become a limiting factor of the number/amount of antibody variants that can be produced and tested. Polyethylenimine (PEI) has proven to be an excellent replacement since it is inexpensive and can be used according to a simple protocol. It was first described by Boussif et al. [17]. The first PEI variant that was successfully used was linear PEI 25 kDa (Polysciences). This PEI is difficult to dissolve since it has to be dissolved in low pH but transfected at neutral pH. Instead, a more easily dissolved variant is used: PEI Max 40 kDa (Polysciences). The same expression levels were obtained with both PEI variants (data not shown), and since PEI max 40 kDa is easier to handle this variant was chosen for the experiments described in this study. steps.title: Amplify and purify plasmid DNA
steps.instruction: Transform the cloned plasmid into TOP10 cells (ThermoFisher) following the supplier's protocol, grow the bacteria in recommended liquid medium with ampicillin, and purify the plasmid using GeneJET endo‑free maxiprep, GeneJET maxiprep, or QIAGEN maxiprep kits as described. Measure DNA concentration with a DeNovix DS‑11 microvolume spectrophotometer and confirm an A260/A280 ratio > 1.8 before transfection.

steps.title: Prepare cells day before transfection
steps.instruction: Ensure Expi293 cells have ≥ 95 % viability and a density ≤ 3–5 million cells · ml⁻¹. Spin the culture at 200 × g for 10 min at room temperature in 225 ml centrifuge tubes (VWR 525‑0506), decant all medium, and resuspend the pellet in pre‑warmed fresh Expi293 medium (use a volume < 50 ml, then dilute as needed) to obtain ~1 million cells · ml⁻¹. For a planned 1000 million‑cell transfection, keep ~600 million cells at this stage. Incubate under standard conditions (37 °C, 5 % CO₂) until the next day.

steps.title: Resuspend cells in transfection medium
steps.instruction: Add Pluronic® F‑68 (VWR A1288.0100) to Expi293 medium to a final concentration of 0.1 % (v/v). Spin the cells again at 200 × g for 10 min at RT, remove the supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in the Pluronic‑containing transfection medium at 20 million cells · ml⁻¹ (e.g., 1000 million cells in 50 ml). Use a 125 ml flask for this volume.

steps.title: Add DNA and PEI to cells
steps.instruction: Add 1.25 mg plasmid DNA per 1000 million cells (for bispecific antibodies use 70 % light‑chain plasmid and 30 % heavy‑chain plasmid). Mix the DNA with the cell suspension, then add 3.75 ml of 1 mg · ml⁻¹ linear 40 kDa PEI Max (Polysciences 24765‑1) per 1000 million cells. Incubate the mixture under standard conditions for 3 h.

steps.title: Dilute culture and add VPA
steps.instruction: Transfer the transfected culture to a larger flask and add pre‑warmed Expi293 medium to reach 1 million cells · ml⁻¹ (e.g., add 950 ml to the 50 ml transfection mixture to make 1 L). Add 0.5 M valproic acid (Sigma‑Aldrich P4543) to a final concentration of 3.5 mM (7 ml per 1 L). Incubate the cells for 7–12 days at 37 °C, 125 rpm, 8 % CO₂ without further handling.

steps.title: Monitor cell viability
steps.instruction: The day after transfection, assess cell viability with a cell counter or microscope (typically 80–95 %). Continue checking viability every few days throughout the culture period.

steps.title: Sample media for expression analysis
steps.instruction: Collect aliquots of the culture supernatant at regular intervals, spin each sample at 13 000 × g for 5 min, and analyse the clarified supernatant by indirect ELISA using the appropriate antigen to determine antibody expression levels.

steps.title: Purify antibodies from supernatant
steps.instruction: Filter the harvested supernatant and load it onto a HiTrap Protein G HP 5 ml column (GE Healthcare 17‑0405‑01) using an ÄKTA start system. Equilibrate the column with PBS (binding buffer) and elute antibodies with 0.7 % acetic acid (elution buffer) while monitoring absorbance at 280 nm. For non‑Fc, His‑tagged proteins, use a 5 ml HisTag Excel column (GE Healthcare Life Sciences 17‑3712‑05) compatible with the chelators present in Expi293 medium.

steps.title: Determine protein concentration
steps.instruction: Measure the purified antibody concentration on a DeNovix DS‑11 spectrophotometer using the A280 setting. Calculate the exact concentration using the extinction coefficient derived from the protein sequence via the Expasy ProtParam tool.
